Save and Restore IsoformicExperiment Objects as Parquet

Source: R/IsoformicExperiment-io.R
isoformic-io.Rd

write_isoformic() writes an IsoformicExperiment to a directory of Parquet files and read_isoformic() restores it. The layout is:

<path>/
  experiment.parquet        key/value: experiment_name, annot_path,
                            isoformic_version, written_at
  col_data.parquet          sample metadata
  metadata.parquet          key/value: scalar entries of `metadata`
  tx_type_palette.parquet   transcript_type, color
  assays/<name>.parquet     transcript_id + one column per sample
  gene_assays/<name>.parquet  only explicitly set gene assays
  dea/det.parquet, dea/deg.parquet, dea/cutoffs.parquet
  dea/uncertainty.parquet, dea/ambiguity.parquet, dea/confidence.parquet
  gsea/<name>.parquet       list columns joined with ";"
  inf_reps/draw_0001.parquet, ...  one draw: transcript_id + samples
  inf_reps/moments/mean.parquet, var.parquet  replicate moments
  annotation/               copy of the annotation directory (optional)

Each file is written only when the object holds that part. Entries of metadata that are not single values are dropped with a warning.

The inferential replicates (self@metadata$inf_reps, see read_inferential_replicates() and add_uncertainty()) are written to inf_reps/: one Parquet file per draw (draw_0001.parquet, ...) with transcript_id and one column per sample, and, when the replicates have a moments attribute, its mean and var matrices in inf_reps/moments/. Their number, their type (the samp_type attribute) and the number of draws behind the moments are recorded in metadata.parquet under the keys inf_reps_n_draws, inf_reps_samp_type and inf_reps_moments_n; when replicates are written, these keys replace entries of metadata with those names, with a warning. One draw is written, and read, at a time, so memory holds the replicates and a single draw on top of them. The replicates of a subset (x[i, j] shares the draws of x and records a selection, see IsoformicExperiment) are written as the selected transcripts and samples only, and the moments as the selected samples. read_isoformic() restores the list of matrices with its samp_type and moments attributes, as they were (including the storage mode of the matrices and of n); for a subset, as plain matrices of the selected draws, without the selection. Only these are kept: names of the draws, other attributes of the list or of the matrices and names of their dimnames are dropped, with a warning. Replicates that are not numeric matrices with transcript and sample names are not written, with a warning. Directories written by earlier versions have no inf_reps/ and are read without replicates. Use add_uncertainty(keep_draws = FALSE), or remove metadata$inf_reps, to save an object without its replicates.

With copy_annotation = TRUE the annotation directory is copied inside the experiment directory so that the result is self-contained and portable. The cached ORF table (annot_data_orfs.parquet) is left out of the copy and computed again when needed. An annotation that lies inside the directory being replaced is always copied, and so is an annotation directory under tempdir() (such as the private copy made by example_isoformic()) when path is not under tempdir() itself: the temporary directory is removed when the R session ends. A message says so. Otherwise annot_path is stored as an absolute path and must still exist when the object is read back (it can be overridden with the annot_path argument of read_isoformic()). Without that argument, read_isoformic() uses an annotation/ directory inside path whenever there is one.

The new directory is built next to path and moved in place at the end, so a failed write leaves an existing experiment as it was. With overwrite = TRUE, a non-empty path is replaced only when it holds an experiment.parquet file.

Usage

write_isoformic(
  self,
  path = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  copy_annotation = FALSE,
  ...
)

read_isoformic(path, annot_path = NULL)

Arguments

self

An IsoformicExperiment.

path

Directory to write to or read from. For write_isoformic() defaults to the object's data_path, or to get_isoformic_cache("experiments", experiment_name).

overwrite

Logical, replace an existing directory.

copy_annotation

Logical, copy the annotation directory inside path.

...

Not used; reserved for methods.

annot_path

Optional annotation directory overriding the stored one when reading.

Value

write_isoformic() returns the object with data_path set, invisibly. read_isoformic() returns an IsoformicExperiment.

Examples

iso <- example_isoformic()
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "iso_example")
iso <- write_isoformic(iso, dir, overwrite = TRUE, copy_annotation = TRUE)
list.files(dir, recursive = TRUE)
#>  [1] "annotation/annot_data_exons.parquet"      
#>  [2] "annotation/annot_data_genes.parquet"      
#>  [3] "annotation/annot_data_sequences.parquet"  
#>  [4] "annotation/annot_data_transcripts.parquet"
#>  [5] "annotation/annot_metadata.parquet"        
#>  [6] "annotation/annot_seq_regions.parquet"     
#>  [7] "assays/abundance.parquet"                 
#>  [8] "assays/counts.parquet"                    
#>  [9] "col_data.parquet"                         
#> [10] "dea/deg.parquet"                          
#> [11] "dea/det.parquet"                          
#> [12] "experiment.parquet"                       
#> [13] "metadata.parquet"                         
#> [14] "tx_type_palette.parquet"                  
iso2 <- read_isoformic(dir)
identical(tx_assay(iso), tx_assay(iso2))
#> [1] TRUE
